messages.author: 23a2cb256755f4e1
messages.subject: question on arguments for   tiles.myobj
parts:
Hi, I'm comparing methylation at CpGs for two samples with 2 replicates each. I'm following this pipeline

1)   read my data (create myobj)
2)   select CpG covered in all replicates for both samples         > meth=unite(myobj, destrand=TRUE)
3)   I subset the methylBase object by coverage                       > meth[meth$coverage1>7 & meth$coverage2>7 & meth$coverage3>7 & meth$coverage4>7]
4)   I calculate diff in meth at base resolution                            >  myDiff <- calculateDiffMeth(meth, num.cores=4);
5)  I print results

But at this point I want to continues with the pipeline, I want to have result calculated in tiles..then I decided to

6)  Tile my object...but at this point I'm not complete sure what to tile. I guess that the command is: 
                                                                                                  > tiles.myobj <- tileMethylCounts(meth, win.size=200, step.size = 200);
              
        IT IS OK TO TILE THE methylBase object "meth"????

7) THen I want to campare methylation at the tiles, and I'm doing    > myDiff <- calculatedDiffMeth(tiles.myobj)

        IT IS THAT RIGHT?  IS tiles.myobj  a different object containing methyl counts in tiles?

PLEASE HELP

ALEJANDRO

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] question on arguments for tiles.myobj
parts:
But at this point I want to continues with the pipeline, I want to have result calculated in tiles..then I decided to

6)  Tile my object...but at this point I'm not complete sure what to tile. I guess that the command is: 
                                                                                                  > tiles.myobj <- tileMethylCounts(meth, win.size=200, step.size = 200);
              
        IT IS OK TO TILE THE methylBase object "meth"????

Yes, you can do that, but you should use the development version, there was a bug with tiling methylBase object in the current version as far as I remember. But keep in mind when you tile the methylBase object, you are using the CpGs that exist in all the samples in your case.

7) THen I want to campare methylation at the tiles, and I'm doing    > myDiff <- calculatedDiffMeth(tiles.myobj)

        IT IS THAT RIGHT?  IS tiles.myobj  a different object containing methyl counts in tiles?

Yes, that works as well. I don't completely understand the second part of your question. "tiles.myobj" should contain methylated and unmethylated base counts on each tile for each sample

 

PLEASE HELP

ALEJANDRO
